description: Portable GraphQL processor scenarios for the closed load gates and confinement (§3.2), pinned-schema interpretation and live introspection (§3.3), and the staleness posture (§4). Peer shape for this family: `peer` is one scripted HTTP response `{status, contentType, body}`, or `{"sequence": [...]}` listing consecutive responses consumed in dispatch order; an entry `{"noResponse": true}` scripts a request that yields no response (connection, name-resolution, or TLS failure, or timeout). Observation paths: `/dispatch` is the last request the processor sent (`method`, `headers`, `body`, `url`), `/dispatches/<i>` the i-th request in order; `/outputs` the emitted operation values in order. Scenarios for §9 arrive with that section. Header field names in dispatch observations are compared case-insensitively, as RFC 9110 section 5.1 makes them; the spellings here are the ones the specification writes. A supplied input carrying a lone surrogate, which §8's JSON-text pin refuses before dispatch, is not scenarioed here because format @1 carries no input materialization; it is a stated gap of this file, not of the rule.

scenarios.description: A location whose scheme is neither http nor https refuses at load, before any request.
A content object without a document member refuses at load.
A document that does not parse under the governing edition's grammar refuses at load.

content.document: query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id name }

scenarios.description: A subscriptions member whose transport and location scheme do not pair refuses at load.
A schema that references an undefined type fails the schema-validity gate and refuses at load.

content.document: query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id } }
content.schema: type Query { viewer(id: ID!): Person }

scenarios.description: A document whose every operation definition shares its name with another leaves no addressable target; the source refuses as a source at resolution.

content.document:
query A { status }
query A { status }

scenarios.description: A duplicated name destroys only the duplicated position's addressability; §5.2.2.1's failure is inventory-wide, so the sibling Status resolves and refuses before dispatch.
A structural introspection member (fields on User) absent at an element the selected operation reaches makes that operation invalid: it refuses before dispatch.
The same structural absence does not reach an operation that never touches the element: Status dispatches against the same pinned result.
An annotative member (isDeprecated on Query.viewer) absent at a reached element makes the operation lossy, not invalid: it dispatches with the carried document and variables unchanged.

A pinned October 2021 result lacks isOneOf on every element and is read as that edition's result: Filter is an ordinary input object, and an invocation carrying two of its members is dispatched; the binding never validates the supplied map against input, so the dispatch is the same under either reading and the OneOf limit of §3.3 is observable only in the emitted schema.
An introspection result whose queryType names a type absent from types references an undefined type: it fails the schema-validity gate and refuses at load.

With schema absent the processor sends exactly the capability probe by POST, then the introspection query composed from every capability the probe observed, then the operation; with every capability observed the composed query is the listed query's bytes exactly.

assertions.equals: query { t: __type(name: "__Type") { fields { name args { name } } } f: __type(name: "__Field") { fields { name args { name } } } d: __type(name: "__Directive") { fields { name args { name } } } i: __type(name: "__InputValue") { fields { name } } }

scenarios.description: A June 2018 service: every probe position observes only the base members, so the composed query carries none of the later additions and no includeDeprecated argument on args or inputFields; the 2018-shaped result lacks isRepeatable and the __InputValue deprecation members, which the edition exceptions read as false and null.

A probe position that resolves to null selects the base selection for that type whatever the other positions observed: with t null, the composed query omits the __Type additions but keeps isRepeatable from d.
A request error result from the probe refuses the source at load, at gate 4; the composed query is never sent.
An execution result whose data is null from the composed query refuses the source at load, at gate 4.
Both introspection requests carry the configured protocolFields the invocation will carry, and remain POST when httpMethod selects get.
Both introspection requests carry the configured extensions map, so the schema observed is the one the invocation's request reaches.

A pinned schema is dispatched against as carried: the processor sends no introspection request, and a service that rejects the pin-validated document produces its own request error, which completes the invocation unsuccessfully with no output.

A service that has evolved beyond the pin returns a value the pinned contract does not admit; the invocation completes with that value as the operation's value (the second staleness face), and no re-introspection is attempted.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema:
type Query { status: Status }
enum Status { ACTIVE }

scenarios.description: Gate 5 applies to a live-introspected result as to a carried one: a live result whose queryType names a type absent from types refuses the source at load, and the operation is never sent.

A June 2018 introspection shape declares interfaces null on an INTERFACE element; that null is the sixth edition exception, read as the empty set, so an operation selecting through the interface is represented and dispatches; no derivation of §5 to §7 reads interfaces on an INTERFACE element, so the exception is presently observable only as the absence of a structural-absence refusal.

content.document: query NodeQ($id: ID!) { node(id: $id) { id } }

scenarios.description: A composed-query result that carries an errors entry beside data.__schema fails gate 4 exactly as a carried object would, and the source refuses at load.
A probe request that yields no response reaches no gate: the load does not complete and the invocation refuses before dispatch for want of an interpreted schema, with no further request.
An operation reaches __Schema.directives through a directive used in a fragment it spreads: with directives absent from the pinned result, A is invalid and refuses before dispatch.
The sibling operation B uses no directive at any of its positions, so the absent directives member has no consequence for it and it dispatches.
With content.subscriptions absent, a subscription operation is accounted invalid for want of a target; its selector resolves and the invocation refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

scenarios.description: The same source's query operation is unaffected by the absent subscriptions member and dispatches.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

assertions.equals:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }

scenarios.description: Loading precedes every refusal below it: a schema-absent source is introspected (probe and composed query) even though the selected subscription, lacking a content.subscriptions target, then refuses before dispatch with no operation request.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }

scenarios.description: A present selector resolves to the operation definition of that exact name and dispatches.
An absent selector over a lone anonymous operation resolves to it and dispatches.

content.document: { status }

scenarios.description: An absent selector over a document holding several operation definitions is ambiguous: no lone operation exists, so the invocation refuses at resolution although every definition remains addressable by name.
A selector naming no operation definition does not resolve: the invocation refuses at resolution.
Names compare by exact code points: a selector differing only in case names no operation definition.
An unused fragment fails §5.5.1.4 and invalidates the whole inventory: a sibling operation resolves and refuses before dispatch.
A directive the interpreted schema does not define fails §5.7.1; the document is sent as carried or not at all, so every operation refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status @connection(key: "s") }
query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id } }

scenarios.description: A directive the interpreted schema defines validates, and the document dispatches with the directive carried as written.

content.document: query Status { status @cache(ttl: 5) }

scenarios.description: A mutation operation against a schema with no mutation root fails §5.2.1.1, which is inventory-wide like every §5 rule: the query sibling refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
mutation Rename($id: ID!, $name: String!) { rename(id: $id, name: $name) { id } }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type User { id: ID! }

scenarios.description: A September 2025 tightening applies to every service: @skip on a subscription's root selection set (§5.2.4.1) invalidates the inventory, so the query sibling refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks @skip(if: false) }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

scenarios.description: A meta-field selection validates against §4.2's introspection types, not the carried type set: it dispatches against a schema whose types omit them.

content.document: query M { __schema { queryType { name } } }

scenarios.description: A service-added validation rule rejects a document this specification accepted: the service's request error is an unsuccessful completion with no output, not a defect.
A string schema omits the built-in directives as §3.13 permits; the interpreted schema still defines @skip, so a document using it validates and dispatches.

content.document: query V($x: Boolean!) { viewer(id: "u-1") { name @skip(if: $x) } }

scenarios.description: A selector naming a name two definitions share does not resolve and refuses at resolution, while the document keeps an addressable sibling so the source is not refused.

content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A string schema that writes a built-in directive itself, here @skip restricted to FIELD, is read as written in place of the built-in: gate 5's duplicate test does not fire and a field-position use validates and dispatches.

content.document: query Status { status @skip(if: false) }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
directive @skip(if: Boolean!) on FIELD

scenarios.description: The written @skip restricted to FIELD governs validation as written: a use on a fragment spread fails §5.7.2 and the inventory is invalid, so the operation refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query S { ...F @skip(if: false) }
fragment F on Query { status }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
directive @skip(if: Boolean!) on FIELD

scenarios.description: A literal at a custom scalar position is treated as coercible (the scalar's rules are the service's), so the document validates and dispatches; the service's answer decides it.

content.document: query Late { events(after: "not-a-date") }
content.schema:
scalar DateTime @specifiedBy(url: "https://scalars.graphql.org/andimarek/date-time")
type Query { events(after: DateTime): Int }

scenarios.description: An Int literal outside the 32-bit range is refused by a service only as a SHOULD, so this specification treats it as coercible and dispatches; a strict service's request error is an unsuccessful completion under §8.

content.document: query Big { f(n: 2147483648) }
content.schema: type Query { f(n: Int): Int }

errors.message: Int cannot represent non 32-bit signed integer value: 2147483648

scenarios.description: A scalar the string schema writes under a built-in name remains that built-in: a String literal at an Int position fails §5.6.1 under §3.5's coercion, the inventory is invalid, and the operation refuses before dispatch.

content.document: query Q { f(n: "123") }
content.schema:
scalar Int
type Query { f(n: Int): Int }

scenarios.description: A widened @oneOf definition the string writes governs only directive validation; the OneOf semantics the edition keys to the name still apply, so an empty input object literal fails §5.6.1 and the operation refuses before dispatch.

content.document: query Q { g(x: {}) }

scenarios.description: A pinned result lacking defaultValue at an argument §5.4.3 reads is an annotative absence: the rule is not evaluated there, the operation reaching it is lossy and dispatches, and a sibling is unaffected.

content.document:
query A { f }
query B { status }

assertions.equals:
query A { f }
query B { status }

scenarios.description: A selector that is not a Name does not resolve: the invocation refuses at resolution.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: An absent selector over a document holding no operation definition does not resolve: the source loads with an empty inventory and the invocation refuses at resolution.

content.document: fragment F on Query { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: The variables map is carried unchanged: an unknown key passes through, an explicit null is sent as null, and an absent key is not invented.
Absent input carries no variables member at all.
The POST request carries exactly the four members, application/json without a parameter, and the pinned Accept value; extensions is absent when not configured.
A configured extensions map is sent verbatim as the request's extensions member.
Under httpMethod get the parameters ride the URL's query component in URLSearchParams form, in the stated order, and the request has no body.

content.document: query Status { status }

scenarios.description: A mutation under httpMethod get refuses before dispatch.
protocolFields header and cookie contributions ride the request: headers as given, cookies as one Cookie field holding their cookie-string.
A contribution naming a reserved or processor-owned field refuses before dispatch.
Two header contributions whose names differ only by ASCII case collide and refuse before dispatch.
A header value that is not an RFC 9110 field-value (it carries CR LF) refuses before dispatch.
A 3xx without the GraphQL media type is not followed: it is any other response and completes unsuccessfully with no output and no second request.
A response carrying application/graphql-response+json is a GraphQL result whatever its status: a 500 with data and no errors completes successfully.
A response carrying application/json is a GraphQL result with a 2xx status.
A non-2xx application/json response is any other response: it completes unsuccessfully with no output.
A charset other than utf-8 makes the response not a GraphQL result.
charset compares ASCII case-insensitively and other parameters are ignored.
An execution result with non-null data and errors emits data as the output value and then completes unsuccessfully (RULING-02).
An execution result with null data and errors carries no value and completes unsuccessfully.
An execution result with null data and no errors has no successful reading and completes unsuccessfully with no output.
An empty errors list is read as absent: data beside it is the operation's value and the invocation completes successfully.
Unknown top-level entries and the extensions entry are ignored.
A request error result (no data entry) completes unsuccessfully with no output.
A response in a non-GraphQL media type completes unsuccessfully with no output.
An operation request that yields no response completes unsuccessfully with no output.
A 303 carrying application/graphql-response+json is classified by media type first: its request error result completes the invocation unsuccessfully, and the Location is never acted on.

The capability probe is §8's POST request: it carries the pinned Accept, a 302 text/html answer is not followed and is not a GraphQL result, so gate 4 refuses the source at load with no further request.
A Content-Type whose value is a list of media types selects no media type: the response is any other response and completes unsuccessfully with no output.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A supplied input value that is not a JSON object refuses before dispatch, whatever JSON type it is.
Cookie-pairs are serialized in ascending code-point order of cookie name, so the Cookie field's value is fixed.
A quoted charset parameter value is unquoted before comparison, so charset="utf-8" is the expected case and the result is a GraphQL result.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: protocolFields are validated after the load gates and before any request: with schema absent, a reserved-field contribution stops the load and the invocation refuses before dispatch with no introspection request sent.

content.document: query Status { status }

scenarios.description: Present input that is an empty map is carried as an empty variables map.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A response carrying no Content-Type is read as application/octet-stream, its data never examined: any other response, completing unsuccessfully with no output.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: An empty errors list beside no data is read as absent first, leaving a body with neither entry: malformed, any other response, unsuccessful with no output.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: An introspection result that omits the built-in scalars and directives, as June 2018 allows, reads them as defined: a document using @include over a String field validates and dispatches.

content.document: query Status($b: Boolean!) { status @include(if: $b) }

scenarios.description: A composed-query result carrying an empty errors list beside data.__schema reads the list as absent before gate 4, exactly as a carried object would: the source loads and the operation dispatches.
The load gates run before protocolFields validation: a source whose location scheme is neither http nor https refuses at load even though a reserved-field contribution is also configured.
A location whose scheme is spelled in uppercase passes gate 1, because RFC 3986 section 3.1 compares scheme names case-insensitively; the operation dispatches.
A location ending in a question mark carries an empty query component, and a query component of any length refuses at load.

Under httpMethod get, variables and a configured extensions ride the query component as JSON strings after query and operationName, in that order, with no body; the JSON images' bytes vary within §11.4's freedom, so only the fixed parts of the URL are asserted.
A present input that is null is not a map: the invocation refuses before dispatch.
An empty cookies map contributes no Cookie field, since a cookie-string holds at least one pair.

A null in a position §4.2 declares non-null (isDeprecated on a __Field) reads as absent with its class's consequence: an annotative absence, so the operation reaching User.name still dispatches and its schema declares nothing for the member.

A field whose type chain ends in a wrapper with ofType null has no innermost named element: that is a structural absence at the wrapper, not a gate 5 condition, so the source loads, Viewer is invalid, and its invocation refuses before dispatch.
The structural absence of the previous scenario is operation-scoped: Status, which does not reach Query.viewer, dispatches against the same result.
protocolFields validation precedes resolution: with a schema carried, an unresolvable selector, and a reserved-field contribution, the invocation refuses before dispatch, not at resolution.
Present input that is an empty map is carried on GET as a variables parameter, since presence is the same on both lanes.
An innermost reference element whose name is null names nothing gate 5 can test: it is a structural absence at that element, so the source loads and the operation reaching it refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
query Other { other }

scenarios.description: The null-name absence of the previous scenario is operation-scoped: Other, which does not reach Query.status, dispatches against the same result.

content.document:
query Status { status }
query Other { other }

scenarios.description: A pinned result whose chain is truncated at the tenth wrapper, as the listed query's nine-level TypeRef fragment truncates it, carries a structural absence at that wrapper: the operation reaching the field refuses before dispatch and the source stays loaded.

content.document:
query D { deep }
query Status { status }

scenarios.description: A Cookie header contribution beside a present cookies map, even an empty one, refuses before dispatch.
A cookie value that is not an RFC 6265 cookie-value (it carries a semicolon) refuses before dispatch.
A header name that is not an RFC 9110 token (it carries a space) refuses before dispatch.
An httpMethod value outside post and get refuses before dispatch as a configuration the specification does not define.
A body beginning with a byte order mark is not a JSON text under this binding: any other response, unsuccessful with no output.
A body whose string carries an escape denoting a lone surrogate is malformed: no value exists to emit, unsuccessful with no output.
A body carrying a number the runtime cannot represent as a finite value is malformed, unsuccessful with no output.

content.document: query N { n }
content.schema: type Query { n: Float }

scenarios.description: A types entry whose kind is absent is a structural absence at that element, not a gate 5 condition: the source loads and the operation reaching Filter refuses before dispatch.
The kind absence of the previous scenario is operation-scoped: Status, which does not reach Filter, dispatches against the same result.

A structural absence attaches at the element whether or not the operation's derivation reads the member: interfaces absent on the Query element makes Status, which reaches Query, refuse before dispatch.
The supplied map is never validated against input before dispatch: a OneOf input object carrying two members is sent as supplied and the service's answer stands.
A Cookie header contribution with no cookies map is an ordinary header contribution and is sent as given.
